{
  "id": "PUB010",
  "title": "Temperature Logic Control",
  "difficulty": "medium",
  "requirements": "# Temperature Logic Control\n\n- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)\n\n## Requirements\n\nWrite a function block FB to implement a temperature control logic. The program should include the following functions:\n1. Read the value of the temperature sensor through an analog input module.\n2. Compare the read temperature value TemperatureSensorInput with the set temperature value SetTemperature.\n3. If the actual temperature is lower than the set temperature, start the heater HeaterOutput.\n4. If the actual temperature is higher than the set temperature, turn off the heater HeaterOutput.\n5. If the heater works continuously for more than a certain period (for convenience, using 5s), it should trigger an overheating protection, automatically turn off the heater, and must wait for a certain period (for convenience, using 3s) before the overheating protection can be lifted.\n6. Provide status indication, displaying the current temperature, set temperature, heater status, and whether overheating protection is triggered.\n7. Provide temperature sensor fault judgment, if the read temperature value TemperatureSensorInput is less than 0 or greater than 100, it is considered a sensor fault, and the heater should be turned off.\n\n## Interface Definition\n\n| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Input | `TemperatureSensorInput` | `REAL` | The input value of the temperature sensor, i.e., the actual temperature |\n| Input | `SetTemperature` | `REAL` | The set temperature value |\n| Output | `CurrentTemperature` | `REAL` | Display of the current temperature |\n| Output | `SetTempDisplay` | `REAL` | Display of the set temperature |\n| Output | `HeaterStatus` | `BOOL` | Display of the heater status |\n| Output | `OverheatProtection` | `BOOL` | Display of the overheating protection status |\n| Output | `HeaterOutput` | `BOOL` | The control output of the heater |",
  "scenario": "Write a function block FB to implement a temperature control logic. The program should include the following functions:",
  "interface": [
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "TemperatureSensorInput",
      "type": "REAL",
      "description": "The input value of the temperature sensor, i.e., the actual temperature"
    },
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "SetTemperature",
      "type": "REAL",
      "description": "The set temperature value"
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "CurrentTemperature",
      "type": "REAL",
      "description": "Display of the current temperature"
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "SetTempDisplay",
      "type": "REAL",
      "description": "Display of the set temperature"
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "HeaterStatus",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Display of the heater status"
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "OverheatProtection",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Display of the overheating protection status"
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "HeaterOutput",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "The control output of the heater"
    }
  ],
  "initial_conditions": {
    "HeaterOutput": false,
    "HeaterStatus": false,
    "OverheatProtection": false,
    "heatDemand": false,
    "heatElapsed_ms": 0,
    "cooldownElapsed_ms": 0,
    "CurrentTemperature": 0.0,
    "SetTempDisplay": 0.0
  },
  "scan_semantics": "At scan k, inputs I[k] are sampled once, q[k] is pre-scan retained state, outputs O[k] are observed after execution, and q[k+1] is the updated state. Each test creates a fresh FB instance before step 0. An initialized instance has not yet executed a scan. Timer elapsed time is zero on the first eligible sampled invocation; dt_ms is elapsed wall time since the previous invocation, not automatically a synthetic input to the FB. No unobserved past input stability is assumed. All sequences here are expected values.",
  "safety_priority": [
    "Sensor fault or active overheat protection overrides the heat demand.",
    "Protection shutdown is evaluated before the output is finalized."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "At equality TemperatureSensorInput=SetTemperature, retain the last heat-demand state. On a fresh instance the retained demand is FALSE.",
    "The prose says \"more than\" a period and gives 5s. The evaluation resolves this to a 5-second threshold: protection trips at continuous heating elapsed>=5s, beginning with elapsed zero at the first energized sample.",
    "Protection is latched for at least 3s from its trip. At elapsed>=3s it may clear and heat can restart in the same scan if the sensor is valid and demand remains.",
    "A sensor fault immediately turns heat off and resets continuous-heating time. It does not clear or restart an already active cooldown.",
    "The display outputs mirror their corresponding sampled temperature and setpoint even during a fault. HeaterStatus equals HeaterOutput. Inputs are held stable between timed samples.",
    "The task interface, requirements, assumptions, and normalized LTL definitions (excluding reference-only ground truth) are supplied identically to both frameworks. Output names always denote observed candidate outputs, never precomputed expected values.",
    "Evaluation decision: retain the existing >=5s trip threshold as an explicit benchmark interpretation of the source more-than wording; cooldown MUST clear at the first observed elapsed>=3s, though a sensor fault or absent demand still prevents heating. No spontaneous protection is allowed. This benchmark interpretation is not claimed to be instructor clarification.",
    "Floating-point inputs and intermediate reference arithmetic are finite. Existing fixed traces retain their declared absolute tolerance; claims do not extend to arbitrary magnitudes without a separately specified numeric error policy.",
    "Scan k=0 initializes the internal elapsed-time clock at 0 ms (ignoring dt_ms[0]); subsequent scans advance by dt_ms[k]. During sensorFault (TemperatureSensorInput < 0 or > 100), the internal retained heat demand freezes at its prior state.",
    "The task interface, requirements, assumptions, and normalized LTL definitions (excluding reference-only ground truth) are supplied identically to both frameworks. Output names always denote observed candidate outputs, never precomputed expected values."
  ],
  "ltl": [
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P_init",
      "kind": "safety",
      "formula": "init",
      "description": "Before the first scan invocation, all declared OUTPUT variables and initial instance state hold their declared initial values.",
      "explanation": "Applies strictly to the fresh pre-invocation initial instance observation before scan k=0 (INITIAL_INSTANCE scope).",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "INITIAL_INSTANCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P1",
      "formula": "G(sensorFault -> !HeaterOutput)",
      "explanation": "Invalid sensor data must never energize the heater.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P2",
      "formula": "G(OverheatProtection -> !HeaterOutput)",
      "explanation": "The heater remains off during cooldown.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P3",
      "formula": "G(HeaterStatus=HeaterOutput)",
      "explanation": "The status output reports actual commanded heat.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P4",
      "formula": "G((CurrentTemperature=TemperatureSensorInput) & (SetTempDisplay=SetTemperature))",
      "explanation": "The displays mirror sampled values.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P5",
      "formula": "G((!sensorFault & !OverheatProtection & demand & !heatLimitReached) -> HeaterOutput)",
      "explanation": "A permitted heat demand energizes the heater.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P6",
      "formula": "G(heatLimitReached -> (OverheatProtection & !HeaterOutput))",
      "explanation": "The continuous-heating threshold trips protection in the same scan.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P7",
      "formula": "G((protectPrev & !cooldownDone) -> OverheatProtection)",
      "explanation": "Protection cannot clear before its cooldown expires.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P8",
      "formula": "(G(F(TimeTick))) -> (G((OverheatProtection & G(!sensorFault & demand)) -> F(HeaterOutput)))",
      "explanation": "With advancing time and persistent valid demand, heating resumes after finite cooldown. Explicit non-Zeno environment premise: physical elapsed time crosses infinitely many 1ms boundaries.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P9",
      "kind": "safety",
      "formula": "G(!sensorFault & !OverheatProtection & !demand -> !HeaterOutput)",
      "description": "When there is no heat demand, HeaterOutput stays FALSE.",
      "explanation": "Prevents constant-ON or false heating when temperature is at or above setpoint.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P10",
      "kind": "safety",
      "formula": "G(protectPrev & cooldownDone -> !OverheatProtection)",
      "description": "Once at least 3s cooldown has elapsed from trip time, OverheatProtection MUST clear immediately on that scan.",
      "explanation": "Prevents permanent latch-up beyond 3s cooldown.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "PUB010.P11",
      "formula": "G((TemperatureSensorInput>SetTemperature) -> !HeaterOutput)",
      "explanation": "Explicit correction of a demonstrated omission.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    }
  ],
  "atomic_propositions": {
    "sensorFault": "TemperatureSensorInput<0 OR TemperatureSensorInput>100",
    "demand": "Ghost retained demand; when 0<=TemperatureSensorInput<=100, set below SetTemperature, clear above SetTemperature, retain at equality; frozen during sensorFault; initial FALSE.",
    "heatLimitReached": "Continuous energized time has reached 5s, with first energized scan at elapsed zero.",
    "cooldownDone": "When OverheatProtection was previously active, at least 3s has elapsed since its trip timestamp at the current scan clock (clock - protection_start >= 3s).",
    "protectPrev": "{\"kind\": \"previous_observed_output\", \"source\": \"O[k-1].OverheatProtection\", \"initial\": false, \"update\": \"After comparing scan k, store ACTUAL O[k].OverheatProtection; never write into reference state.\"}",
    "interface names": "Identically named sampled input or observed output.",
    "TimeTick": "Boolean: floor(t[k]/1ms)>floor(t[k-1]/1ms), with t[0]=0, TimeTick[0]=FALSE, t[k]=sum(dt_ms[1..k]). G(F(TimeTick)) states unbounded physical time progress; merely positive dt is insufficient.",
    "TemperatureSensorInput": "I[k].TemperatureSensorInput: sampled input (REAL).",
    "SetTemperature": "I[k].SetTemperature: sampled input (REAL).",
    "CurrentTemperature": "O[k].CurrentTemperature: independently observed post-scan candidate value (REAL); never defined as expected output.",
    "SetTempDisplay": "O[k].SetTempDisplay: independently observed post-scan candidate value (REAL); never defined as expected output.",
    "HeaterStatus": "O[k].HeaterStatus: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.",
    "OverheatProtection": "O[k].OverheatProtection: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.",
    "HeaterOutput": "O[k].HeaterOutput: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.",
    "init": "At the separate pre-invocation initial observation before scan k=0: O_init.CurrentTemperature=0.0, O_init.SetTempDisplay=0.0, O_init.HeaterStatus=false, O_init.OverheatProtection=false, O_init.HeaterOutput=false."
  }
}

  "state_machine": [
    {
      "state": "IDLE",
      "meaning": "Heater commanded off; protection inactive.",
      "transitions": [
        "If the sensor is valid and heatDemand is true, enter HEATING and record heatStart as the current scan time.",
        "Otherwise remain IDLE."
      ]
    },
    {
      "state": "HEATING",
      "meaning": "Heater commanded on; continuous heating time starts at zero on entry.",
      "transitions": [
        "If the preceding continuous energized interval has reached 5s, enter PROTECTED and record protectionStart as the current scan time.",
        "Otherwise, if sensorFault is true or heatDemand is false, enter IDLE and reset heating time.",
        "Otherwise remain HEATING."
      ],
      "boundary_rule": "An interval already reaching 5s trips protection even if a fault or loss of demand is sampled on that scan. The fault or loss of demand still turns the heater off and resets heating time."
    },
    {
      "state": "PROTECTED",
      "meaning": "Protection is active and the heater is commanded off.",
      "transitions": [
        "Before 3s from protectionStart, remain PROTECTED regardless of sensor faults or demand changes.",
        "At the first scan at or after 3s, clear protection. Enter HEATING with heatStart set to the current scan time if the sensor is valid and heatDemand is true; otherwise enter IDLE."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "timer_plan": [
    {
      "name": "HeatTON",
      "type": "TON",
      "PT": "T#5s",
      "call": "Call unconditionally once per scan with IN equal to state = HEATING.",

    },
    {
      "name": "CooldownTON",
      "type": "TON",
      "PT": "T#3s",
      "call": "Call unconditionally once per scan with IN equal to state = PROTECTED.",

    },
    {
      "name": "Authoritative scan-time deadlines",
      "type": "Monotonic timestamps",
      "PT": "5s heating; 3s protection",
      "purpose": "Evaluate transitions before the current scan's TON calls, without relying on their stale Q values. Record heatStart and protectionStart on state entry and compare elapsed monotonic time against the respective threshold.",
      "reset": "Discard heatStart on leaving HEATING and protectionStart on leaving PROTECTED.",
      "timing_notes": "Sample a monotonic runtime clock once per scan; normalize the first scan to zero and ignore any pre-invocation interval. Use adequate resolution and wrap-safe elapsed-time arithmetic. The TONs provide elapsed-time diagnostics; timestamp comparisons govern transitions."
    }
  ],
  "priorities": [
    "Sensor fault is TemperatureSensorInput < 0 or TemperatureSensorInput > 100. It prevents heating immediately and freezes heatDemand.",
    "Active protection prevents heating. A fault neither clears nor restarts an active cooldown.",
    "Recognize an already completed 5s energized interval before discarding its heating timestamp; trip protection in that scan.",
    "When valid, set heatDemand below the setpoint, clear it above the setpoint, and retain it at equality, including while protected.",
    "At cooldown expiry, clear protection in that scan; restart heat only if the sensor is valid and demand remains.",
    "Threshold actions occur at observed scans. Task scheduling must be fast enough for the required physical response; a stalled task cannot guarantee shutdown at exactly 5s."

  "initial_values": {

    "sensorFault": false,

    "CurrentTemperature": 0.0,
    "SetTempDisplay": 0.0,
    "HeaterStatus": false,
    "OverheatProtection": false,
    "HeaterOutput": false

  "scan_execution_order": [
    {
      "stage": 1,
      "name": "Edge sampling",
      "actions": "Snapshot both inputs and the monotonic clock once. Retain the prior state for transition detection. No external edge-trigger inputs are required."
    },
    {
      "stage": 2,
      "name": "Safety/reset priority and state transitions",
      "actions": "Compute sensorFault; update or freeze heatDemand. Evaluate the prior state's elapsed timestamp and apply the specified transitions and timestamp resets or entries. Compute elapsed values from the sampled clock. Do not use this scan's timer Q values for transitions."
    },
    {
      "stage": 3,
      "name": "Unconditional top-level timer FB calls",
      "actions": "Outside all CASE and IF blocks, call HeatTON and CooldownTON exactly once using the resulting state and their specified PT values."
    },
    {
      "stage": 4,
      "name": "Unified output assignments",
      "actions": "Assign CurrentTemperature and SetTempDisplay from the sampled inputs. Assign OverheatProtection from state = PROTECTED, HeaterOutput from state = HEATING, and HeaterStatus = HeaterOutput."
    }
  ],
  "formal_assertions": [
    {
      "id": "A1",
      "formula": "G(((TemperatureSensorInput < 0.0) OR (TemperatureSensorInput > 100.0)) -> NOT HeaterOutput)"

      "formula": "G(OverheatProtection -> NOT HeaterOutput)"

CODESYS DIALECT CARDS:
[
  {
    "id": "ton_timer",
    "title": "Standard IEC TON Timer Block Invocation",
    "body": "// Standard IEC TON timer: MUST invoke unconditionally OUTSIDE CASE/IF every scan!\nVAR\n    timer : TON;\n    runTimer : BOOL;\nEND_VAR\n// Control via boolean IN flag (never put timer(...) only inside an IF/CASE arm):\nrunTimer := (state = 1) AND NOT resetCmd;\ntimer(IN := runTimer, PT := T#2s);\nIF timer.Q THEN\n    // Timer expired; timer.ET holds elapsed time\nEND_IF;"
  },
  {
    "id": "case_state_machine",
    "title": "Explicit CASE State Machine Transitions",
    "body": "// 4-Stage Scan Order: 1) Edge sample 2) Reset/priority & CASE state transition\n// 3) Unconditional top-level TON/R_TRIG calls 4) Unified output assignments\nVAR\n    state : INT := 0; // 0=IDLE, 1=RUN, 2=FAULT\nEND_VAR\nIF emergencyStop THEN state := 2; END_IF;\nCASE state OF\n    0: IF startCmd AND NOT fault THEN state := 1; END_IF;\n    1: IF faultCmd THEN state := 2; ELSIF stopCmd THEN state := 0; END_IF;\n    2: IF resetCmd THEN state := 0; END_IF;\n    ELSE state := 0;\nEND_CASE;\noutActive := (state = 1); // Assign outputs unconditionally from current state"
  }
]
